entities.text: Sabbani Pramila vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This petition is filed seeking quashment of the C.C.No.2099 of 2024 on the file of learned III Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class/Special Mobile Court at Nizamabad, against the petitioners/accused Nos.2 & 3.
2.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class/Special Mobile Court at Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Ms.Shruti Bose, learned counsel representing Mr.Nageshwar Rao Pujari, learned counsel for petitioners and Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are facing false allegations and that they have never harassed the defacto complainant and there are no specific allegations levelled against the petitioners.

However, she relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Digmbar and another v. The State of Maharashtra and another, and hence prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

entities.text: Digmbar and another v. The State of Maharashtra and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor submits that the defacto complainant is living with the in-laws as per the statement of LW-1 and the statement further discloses allegations against the petitioners herein and therefore he prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Perused the record.
6. Petitioners are facing allegations under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and the statement of witnesses are a part of record and are subject matter of trial.
The veracity of the witnesses can be tested during the course of trial.

7. However, in view of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners, the presence of the petitioners before the trial court is dispensed with provided that they are represented by a counsel before the trial court on every date of hearing and shall appear before the trial court whenever their presence is required during the course of trial.
8. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
